rulers.name: Sviatoslav I

rulers.name: Yaropolk I

rulers.name: Vladimir the Great

rulers.name: Sviatopolk I
rulers.note: Yaroslav's half-brother; the page gives the war for Kiev 1015-1019, Sviatopolk beaten in 1016 and back with Polish troops in 1018; Yaroslav 'firmly established his rule over Kiev' in 1019.

rulers.name: Yaroslav the Wise
rulers.note: Grand Prince of Kiev 1019-1054; shared Rus' with Mstislav 1024-1036; died 20 February 1054.

region.text: the Drevlians west of Kiev

The Sviatoslav page has the Vyatichi 'attacked and forced to pay tribute' (a campaign dated 966 in the Primary Chronicle) and the Vladimir page has 'in 984, he conquered the Radimichs', so the pages show the same peoples subdued again; the region is the reading of their lands (Severia, the Sozh, the upper Oka).

The page gives no month; Boris II 'was captured by the Byzantines in 971'. Cliopatria keeps the Balkan strip to 979.

ledger.note: 1054: Yaroslav dies and Rus' is divided among his sons. He died on 20 February 1054 at Vyshgorod (Yaroslav page). The Kievan Rus' page lists the division: Iziaslav I Kiev and Novgorod, Sviatoslav II Chernigov and Tmutarakan, Vsevolod I Pereyaslavl and Rostov-Suzdal, Vyacheslav Smolensk, Igor Volhynia, and Polotsk to Iziaslav of Polotsk. The Kievan Rus' page and Cliopatria's 'Kievan Rus'' end the state only in 1240 ('The siege of Kiev in 1240 ... is generally understood as the end'), but Cliopatria draws these principalities from 1056, so the whole land is theirs; the Kiev prince kept a nominal seniority (see notes).

notes:
Rows merged: Cliopatria's 'Rus'' (880-881) and 'Kievan Rus'' (882-1240) share Wikidata Q1108445 and one ruler (Oleg, Novgorod 879, Kiev 882), so they are one state under the earlier slug `rus` (cliopatria_names holds both). There is no kievan-rus.json; other dossiers that name the counterpart 'kievan-rus' (khazaria does, for 965 and 969) mean this dossier.

END DATE (decided here): the dossier ends on 20 February 1054, Yaroslav's death, when his sons divide the land (Kievan Rus' page). Three ends are on the pages: 1054 (the division), 1132 ('Following the death of Mstislav I of Kiev in 1132, the semi-autonomous states were de facto independent', Principality of Kiev page; the Kievan Rus' page: Mstislav was the last ruler to keep a united state and died in 1132) and 1240 (the Kievan Rus' page: "The siege of Kiev in 1240 by the Mongols is generally understood as the end of Kievan Rus'."). Cliopatria's 'Kievan Rus'' 1040-1235 shape is 1.2 M km2 beside the principalities from 1056; subtracting the 1056 principalities leaves 267 cells (about 68,000 km2), so the shape is almost wholly the principalities' land. Ending at 1054 puts the hand-over where the map changes. If the principality dossiers start in 1132 instead of 1054/1056 (the Principality of Kiev infobox says established 1132), move this end to 1132 and the 1040 verdict to 1131; the Kiev prince's nominal seniority over the other princes (1054-1240) is not territory and is not drawn. Cliopatria's principalities begin 1056, so 1055 has no owner except this dossier's 1040 shape (the renderer should hold it through 1055).

Kiev gap: the 1055 year, and the 1054-1056 start of the principality dossiers, belong to the eu-16 principality agents.

Page silent / not settled: the 896 and 900 southward growth of the shape (confidence 1); the 972-980 war of Sviatoslav's sons; whether Chersonesos was returned in 988-989 (the occupation_end is confidence 1); what Poland took in 1018; the left-bank division of 1024-1036 is a loss/gain pair against principality-of-chernigov, whose own dossier starts in 1056 (the counterpart has no matching event before 1056; the renderer may draw it as a lighter-tint co-ruler or leave the shape whole); the Vyatichi (885, 966, 981-982) and Radimichs (885, 984) are subdued several times by the pages. Tartu (1030) is outside every Cliopatria shape. The pre-Oleg Rus' Khaganate is 'a hypothetical polity' with no boundary on its page, so it has no dossier and `predecessors` is empty.

Gazetteer names needed: 'Cherven Cities' (Przemysl, Volodymyr and Cherven, the Rus'-Polish marches, a region), 'Yotvingia' (Sudovia/Yatvingia, Podlachia and the Suwalki area), 'Vyatichi land' (upper Oka). Used instead: places Przemysl and Volodymyr, region Podlachia, admin1 Kaluga, Tula, Orel, Gomel, region Chernigov, Kievan core.

Counterparts without a dossier: Askold and Dir (Kiev), Drevlians, Yotvingians, Pechenegs (pechenegs.json exists), Mstislav's left-bank realm 1024-1036.

Page budget: rus 1-2 and kievan-rus up to 9 (11 for the merged state); ten pages were opened.
